forecaster_note: Long period S swell has filled in and mixed with the easing mid-period stuff — inconsistent but well overhead sets for the exposed banks, with a baseline of head to overhead. Elsewhere expect easier size but still with occasional powerful sets wrapping in. Early offshore W/SW winds see some good surf for breaks that can handle a bit of energy. Winds then trend S/SE but drop lighter through the day and size eases a touch for textured, crumbly surf into the afternoon. — Surfline forecast team

wind.summary: Light W/SW offshore this morning — swings S/SE onshore from around midday.

shark.summary: SharkSmart check pending this refresh — tap to check live detections

days.label: Today
days.note: Big S energy on tap — 567 kJ at dawn easing to 438 by 9am, consistency 100. The catch: it's dead south (184°), which wraps badly into Dee Why. Curl Curl and Long Reef are getting the real size. Light W/SW offshore until the wind swings S/SE around midday — go early.

dee-why.window: 6–10am. Offshore holds until roughly 11am, then S/SE onshore junks it up.
alerts: Dead S at 184° — expect the wrap to be sloppy and the Point to be inconsistent. Long Reef and Curl Curl are the better calls today.

tip.label: Frontside at the Point
tip.text: If you do paddle out at Dee Why, sit wide at the Point and wait for the bigger long-period sets — the 11s stuff is the only thing bending in with any shape. The 8s SE mush will close out on the bank.

long-reef.window: Dawn to 9am while the wind is still light. Biggest of the four by a margin.
alerts: Well overhead sets — solid, powerful and inconsistent. Strong paddle required.

tip.label: Size is here
tip.text: This is the day for the step-up. Cross-shore texture but the sheer size makes it worth it — pick off the long-period sets and let the 8s slop go through.

curl-curl.window: 6–11am. Best combination of size and offshore wind on the coast this morning.

tip.label: Pick of the day
tip.text: Straight offshore over head-high-plus banks. Beachie so it'll be shifty — pick the peak that's holding the 11s energy and commit early on the drop.

manly.window: Any time before midday — but it's the smallest option today.
alerts: Heavily shadowed from the S swell — half the size of everywhere else.

tip.label: Fallback only
tip.text: Clean and offshore but waist-to-chest. Only worth it if you want an easy one — the energy is all going to the north corners today.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: Size backs off but quality steps up. New long-period S swell (18s) fills in underneath the 12s, energy 250 kJ, consistency down to 77 so expect waiting. Offshore W/NW until roughly 11am, then NE onshore. Curl Curl rated fair-good — the mid-morning window is yours.

long-reef.window: Dawn to 11am. Still holding the most size.

curl-curl.window: 9–11am is the sweet spot — offshore, chest-to-head, and it lines up with your usual mid-morning slot.

manly.window: Early only — drops to poor-fair once the NE arrives.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Saturday is the better half — 250 kJ and offshore mornings. Sunday the energy collapses to 99 kJ but a clean 18s long-period S lingers, so the south-facing banks still produce chest-to-head sets early. Both days the wind turns NE by lunch and hard NE (22 km/h) Sunday afternoon. Long Reef rated fair-good Sunday morning is the standout.

dee-why.window: Both mornings before 11am. Sunday afternoon goes poor with 22 km/h NE.
alerts: Swell stays dead S (182–185°) all weekend — Dee Why keeps under-performing its neighbours.

long-reef.window: Sunday 6–9am is rated fair-good with offshore wind — best window of the weekend.

curl-curl.window: Saturday mid-morning is the pick; Sunday early only before the NE fills.

manly.window: Small both days — early sessions only.
alerts: Shadowed all weekend by the S direction.
